entities.summary:
Eperatus of Pharae in Achaea was an ancient Greek general of the 3rd century BC. He served as a prominent military commander under the Macedonian king Antigonus I Monophthalmus, leading key campaigns in Asia Minor and the Mediterranean.

Eperatus' most notable achievement was his victory at the Battle of Magnesia in 190 BC, where he successfully repelled an invasion by the Seleucid Empire. This victory not only secured Macedonian dominance in the region but also cemented Eperatus' reputation as a skilled and courageous commander.

Despite his significant military contributions, Eperatus' legacy is somewhat overshadowed by the rise of Alexander the Great, who succeeded Antigonus I and went on to conquer much of the known world. Nevertheless, Eperatus' achievements played a crucial role in shaping the trajectory of Hellenistic power in the region.

As a testament to his enduring impact, Eperatus' name has been preserved in the annals of history, serving as a reminder of the complex and often brutal realities of ancient warfare.
